notes:
**Job cards and run cards.** Recurring work can live on a card. Tap a job card on the machine's
reader (or scan its QR code) and the job opens; tap a run card and it opens and starts printing,
after a short countdown you can cancel that says exactly what is about to print. Cards can resume
where a job left off or start it from the beginning.

**Card packs that need nothing written.** Cards from TNR come ready to use: tap a new one and
Studio asks which job it belongs to - the job on screen or any saved job - and from then on it
just works. Hand one to each operator; the Home tab shows which card opens which job.

**Tags & QR Codes.** File > Tags & QR Codes makes the codes yourself: write an NFC card through the
machine's reader, or print the same code as a QR label from a small label window with the pen
bands, copies and ink profile right there. Ink cartridges, jobs and supply items alike.

**Scan to order.** With the order form open, scanning an ink cartridge or a supply adds it to the
order - scan again to add another.

**Kiosk mode.** File > Kiosk Mode gives a shop-floor PC one calm screen: the printer's status and
"Tap a card to start". It can be the page Studio opens on.

**A default ink profile.** Ink Profiles > Set as default picks the profile a new job starts with;
the installer's new Ink profile page sets it on a fresh machine. A profile saved in a job always
wins.

**Spoken confirmations, if you want them.** Settings > Scanner > Speak scan events has Studio say
what a scan did - "Opening Bag Labels", "Solv-1832 ink applied" - for the operator at the feeder.
Off unless you turn it on.

**Smaller things.** The properties panel keeps its captions readable on narrow screens; the
high-DPI checks the installer runs before every build now give the same answer on every machine.
